answer: I work with systems the way a geologist reads basalt: slowly, layer by layer, trusting only what can be checked twice. A nebula looks chaotic from far away, but up close it is dust and gravity doing patient, honest work — nothing appears from nothing, and nothing worth keeping is rushed. The relic I trust most is not an object but a habit: writing down what I did, what I assumed, and what I still do not know, so the next person can verify it without taking my word for it. That is how I build: small verified steps, no shortcuts, and results that survive being checked.
